It is unclear whether the vertical stroke under aleph in אָֽתָּה is a meteg.
The second letter in the small print could be final mem (ע״ם) or samekh (ע״ס). The intended reading is probably ע״ס א״ב (על סדר אלף בית). The text above records the letter as it appears.
The left half is tightly set, with little or no space between words (looks like לְוָתִיקוְעֹשֶׂהחֶסֶד). The word breaks above are inferred.
It is unclear whether וְעֹשֶׂה is defective (holam over ayin) or plene וְעוֹשֶׂה. The scan looks defective.
There is a small mark over ה in לְהוֹגֶה. It may be a meteg, an accent, or a print speck.

The first letter of the last word in the right half looks somewhat like kaf (כַּדִּין) and not bet. The expected reading is בַּדִּין. If it is kaf, it is a print artifact or a source typo; proposed correction: בַּדִּין.
The pointing of שָׁ in מַחֲשָׁבוֹת is partly obscured by a mark above the shin.
As in row 05, the first letter of the last word in the right half could be read as kaf (כַּדִּין). The expected reading is בַּדִּין.

Every אבינו/מלכנו in the footnote looks literally like אביט/מלכט in Rashi script (נו is ligature-like). I transcribed them as אבינו/מלכנו.
